stages.title: Language sounds and pronunciation
explain: French has nasal vowels. In "bon" and "pain" the air goes through your nose, and the final n is not said as a separate sound.
Many final letters are silent. In "petit" you do not say the t, and in "chat" you do not say the t either. The letter h is also silent, as in "homme".

gq.q: In "chat", what happens to the final letter t?
gq.why: Most final consonants in French are not pronounced.

gq.q: Which word has a nasal vowel?
gq.why: In "bon" the vowel is said through the nose and the n is not pronounced.

panel.q: Why do we say "l'ami" and not "le ami"?
o: Le drops its vowel before a vowel sound
Because le is only used for animals
panel.why: French avoids two vowel sounds meeting, so le becomes l' with an apostrophe.

panel.q: The word "homme" starts with h. How is it said?
o: With a strong h like in English
panel.why: The French h is silent.

panel.q: Why can "pain" and "paon" feel hard to tell apart for a beginner?
o: Both use nasal vowels that are not like English
Both end in a said n
Both are said with a strong r
panel.why: Nasal vowels have no English equivalent, so learners must train the ear.

teach.model: A nasal vowel is a vowel said with air through the nose. In bon and pain you do not say a clear n at the end. Also many last letters are silent, like the t in chat.

stages.hook: Say "le chat" and "la maison". Do the words sound like they look?
stages.mnemonic: Silent ends, nasal friends: bon, pain, vin.

stages.title: Alphabet, script or basic characters
explain: French uses the Latin alphabet, but letters have French names. For example, "e" is said like "euh" and "g" is said like "zhay".
Accents change the sound or the meaning. é says "ay", è says "eh", ç says "s", and ê also says "eh". In "où" (where) and "ou" (or) the accent changes the meaning.

gq.q: What does the cedilla in "garçon" do?
o: It makes c sound like s
It makes c sound like k
It makes c sound like ch
gq.why: Ç is said /s/ before a, o and u.
The accent in où separates it from ou, which means "or".

panel.q: In "école", which accent mark is used and what does it sound like?
panel.why: The acute accent gives the sound /e/, close to English "ay".

panel.q: Why is "ou" without an accent different from "où"?
o: They are different words with different meanings
One is only written, one only spoken
panel.why: The accent separates two words, "or" and "where".

panel.q: Why can a missing accent cause a real mistake in French?
o: It can change the sound and sometimes the word
It only matters in capital letters
panel.why: Accents are part of the spelling, so leaving them out may alter meaning.

points.ask: Do ou and où mean the same?

teach.model: French has five accents. They can change how a letter sounds, like é and è, or change the word, like ou and où. The cedilla makes c sound like s.

stages.hook: The French alphabet has the same 26 letters as English. So why do the names of the letters sound so different?
stages.mnemonic: Accents are small hats and tails that tell you how to say the letter.

stages.title: Greetings and introductions
explain: Say "bonjour" in the day and "bonsoir" in the evening. With friends you can say "salut". To say goodbye, say "au revoir".
To say your name, say "Je m'appelle" and your name. To ask someone's name, say "Comment tu t'appelles?" with a friend. People in France often kiss on the cheek, but a handshake is common too.

gq.q: Which greeting is best with a teacher you do not know?
gq.why: Bonjour is polite and works in all situations.

gq.q: You meet someone at night. What do you say?

panel.q: Why is it "Je m'appelle" and not "Je me appelle"?
o: Me drops its vowel before a vowel sound
It is only a spoken shortcut
panel.why: Words like me, le and je drop their vowel before a vowel sound, which is written with an apostrophe.

panel.q: What is the difference between "tu" and "vous" in greetings?
o: Tu is for friends, vous is polite or plural
Tu is plural, vous is singular
panel.why: French marks formality and plurality with these two pronouns.

panel.q: Why does it sound odd to say "Salut" to a stranger in an office?
o: It is too informal for that setting
It is rude in every setting
panel.why: Register matters: salut is for friends and family.

points.ask: How do I say my name?

teach.model: Say bonjour to greet people in the day, bonsoir in the evening, and salut to friends. Say au revoir to leave. To give your name say Je m'appelle.

stages.hook: How do you say hello to a friend and to your teacher in French? Is it the same?
stages.mnemonic: Bonjour is "good day": bon is good, jour is day.

stages.title: Numbers and counting
explain: Count: un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix. Be careful: the last letter of "cinq" is said, but the t of "huit" is said too. In "trois ans" a z sound links the two words.
The numbers 11 to 16 are special: onze, douze, treize, quatorze, quinze, seize. After that, dix-sept means 17. Tens are vingt (20), trente (30), quarante (40).

gq.why: In French the tens come first: dix-sept.

panel.q: How do French speakers say their age?
o: Elle a dix ans, literally "she has ten years"
panel.why: French uses avoir for age.

panel.q: Why is "trois ans" said with a z sound between the words?
o: Liaison links the s of trois to the vowel in ans
panel.why: A silent final consonant is pronounced before a vowel in set expressions.

panel.q: Which number is a natural cause of confusion for English speakers, six or cinq?
o: Cinq, because the final q is said
Cinq, because it has a z
panel.why: The word cinq looks silent but its final q sounds like k; confusion is a typical learner error.

points.ask: How do I count to three?

teach.model: French numbers go un, deux, trois up to dix. Then onze, douze, treize, quatorze, quinze, seize. After that, dix-sept, dix-huit, dix-neuf, then vingt.

stages.hook: Can you count to ten in French? Which numbers sound like English ones?
stages.mnemonic: Un, deux, trois: one, two, three; count to dix and you are free.

stages.title: Colours and shapes
explain: Colours are adjectives. They usually come after the noun: "une voiture rouge" is a red car. The colour changes with the noun: "un chat noir" and "une chatte noire".
Common colours are rouge, bleu, vert, jaune, noir, blanc, orange. Shapes are un cercle, un carré, un triangle.

gq.q: Where does the colour word usually go?
o: At the end of the sentence
gq.why: French colours normally follow the noun, as in une voiture rouge.

gq.q: Choose the correct form: une fleur ___
gq.why: Fleur is feminine singular, so blanc becomes blanche.

panel.q: Why is it "une maison blanche" but "un mur blanc"?
o: Adjectives agree with the gender of the noun
panel.why: Feminine nouns usually take the feminine form of the adjective.

panel.q: What does it mean to say a colour "agrees" with the noun?
o: It changes to match gender and number
panel.why: Agreement is a main idea in French grammar.

panel.q: Why do "orange" and "marron" often stay unchanged in "des chaussures orange"?
o: They come from nouns, so they are invariable
panel.why: Colours that come from fruit or objects often do not take agreement.

points.ask: What do I do for feminine words?

teach.model: Colours go after the noun in French: un ballon rouge. They change to match the noun. A girl noun gets an extra e, like une maison blanche.

stages.hook: What colour is the sky, the grass and the sun in French? And do colour words change?
stages.mnemonic: Rouge is red like a rose; jaune is the sun.

stages.title: Family and people
explain: Family words: la mère (mother), le père (father), le frère (brother), la sœur (sister). Children say "maman" and "papa".
"Mon" goes with masculine words: mon père. "Ma" goes with feminine words: ma mère. For plural, say "mes parents". Grandparents are les grands-parents.

gq.why: Sœur is feminine, so we use ma.
Parents is plural, so use mes.

panel.q: Why do we say "mon amie" and not "ma amie"?
o: Before a vowel sound mon is used even for feminine nouns
Because ma is only for adults
panel.why: Mon is used before a vowel sound to avoid two vowels meeting.

panel.q: What do "grand-mère" and "grand-père" show about hyphens?
o: Compound family words are joined with a hyphen
panel.why: Hyphenation is part of these compound nouns.

panel.q: Why is "l'enfant" the same for a girl and a boy?
o: Enfant is the same for both genders and the article only elides
French has no word for girl
panel.why: Some nouns do not change form for gender.

points.ask: How do I say mum and dad?
Why are there three words for my?

teach.model: In French each family word has a gender. Use mon for masculine words, ma for feminine and mes for plural. For example mon père, ma mère, mes parents.

stages.hook: Who is in your family? Do you say "my mum" the same way as "my dad"?
stages.mnemonic: Mon père, ma mère, mes parents: mon, ma, mes.

stages.title: Common objects
explain: Every French noun has a gender: masculine or feminine. Use "un" or "le" for masculine and "une" or "la" for feminine. For example, un livre, une table.
In the plural we use "des" and "les": des livres, les tables. The s at the end is usually silent.
sentences: The book is on the table.

gq.why: Table is feminine, so we say la table.
Chaise is feminine, so une is correct.

panel.q: How do you tell a noun's gender?
o: You learn it with the article
panel.why: Gender is usually learned with the word, since few rules are sure.

panel.q: Why does "les livres" sound the same as "le livre" except for the article?
o: The plural s is silent; the article shows the number
There is no plural in French
panel.why: Spoken French marks plural mostly through the article.

panel.q: Why does "le" become "l'" in "l'école" even though école is feminine?
o: Elision depends on a vowel sound, not gender
panel.why: Le and la both drop their vowel before a vowel sound.

teach.model: French nouns are masculine or feminine. Use un or le for masculine and une or la for feminine. Learn the article with each new word.

stages.hook: Look around you. Can you name five things in French?
stages.mnemonic: Un livre, une table: each thing has a gender label.

stages.title: Everyday actions
explain: Many French verbs end in -er. For je, drop -er and add -e: je mange, je joue, je parle. For tu add -es, and for il or elle add -e.
Two key verbs are être (to be) and avoir (to have): je suis, tu es, il est, and j'ai, tu as, il a. For "we", say "nous" and add -ons: nous mangeons.

gq.why: With tu, regular -er verbs end in -es.

panel.q: Why does "manger" add an e in "nous mangeons"?
o: To keep the soft g sound before o
Because it is irregular in all forms
panel.why: Without e the g would sound hard before o.

panel.q: Why is "il parle" and "ils parlent" said the same?
panel.why: Written plural endings are often silent in spoken French.

panel.q: What is wrong with "je suis un faim"?
o: Un must be removed and suis kept
panel.why: French says "I have hunger", so use avoir.

teach.model: Take a verb in -er and remove the ending. Add -e for je, -es for tu and -e for il or elle. Add -ons for nous. For example je parle, tu parles, nous parlons.

stages.hook: What do you do every day? Can you say "I eat, I play, I run" in French?
stages.mnemonic: Je -e, tu -es, il -e: three endings in a row.

stages.title: Simple listening and speaking
explain: In French the words flow together. This is called liaison: a normally silent last consonant is said before a vowel. For example, "les amis" sounds like "lez ami".
French sentences also have a steady rhythm, and the last syllable is slightly longer. To practise, listen for key words like bonjour, merci, oui, non, and repeat them aloud.

o: A normally silent final consonant is said before a vowel
gq.why: In "les amis" the s sounds like z.
Only les amis has a vowel sound after a final s.

panel.q: Why is there no liaison in "les héros"?
o: The h is aspirated, so no liaison
panel.why: Aspirated h blocks liaison and elision.

panel.q: How can you ask a speaker to slow down politely?
panel.why: This uses the polite imperative and s'il vous plaît.

panel.q: Why is listening for liaison useful in understanding speech?
o: It shows where words start and end
panel.why: Liaison links words, so recognising it helps split the stream of sounds.

points.ask: How do I ask someone to repeat?
How do I ask for slow speech?

teach.model: In French, words blend together. A silent last consonant can be said before a vowel, so les amis sounds like lez ami. To understand, listen for key words and ask people to repeat.

stages.hook: Listen closely. When people talk fast in French, how do you know where one word ends?
stages.mnemonic: Liaison is a bridge: a silent letter wakes up before a vowel.
